heroHeadline: Blue Origin Blue Moon Mk2 Lander Mockup Now at NASA JSC; SpaceX IFT-12 Launch Window Opens May 12
heroSubtitle: May 11: NASA began crew training on Blue Origin's full-scale Blue Moon Mark 2 engineering mockup installed at Johnson Space Center's Space Vehicle Mockup Facility — the first hands-on HLS Option B training milestone ahead of Artemis IV's 2028 crewed lunar landing. The mockup (15+ ft tall) enables ingress/egress procedures, suit-to-lander interface drills, and emergency scenario training. SpaceX IFT-12 (Starship V3 — Booster 19 + Ship 39) launch window opens tomorrow May 12 at 22:30 UTC from Starbase Orbital Launch Pad 2; the first V3 flight will test docking port and propellant-transfer hardware critical for Artemis III HLS qualification. Day 31 post-splashdown: Orion visual heat shield inspection continues at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; formal Marshall X-ray scans remain scheduled for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage VAB integration advancing. Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) continue week-5 physiological reconditioning at JSC. Artemis Accords at 67 nations; Indonesia publicly weighing potential 68th signature.
